Abundance scales in preprocessing and quality control

data_scales.Rd

Glyclean reads scale from experiment metadata. An absent field defaults to "raw"; explicitly invalid values are rejected. "log" is the natural logarithm, while "log2" and "log10" use their named bases. "logx" denotes log-like coordinates whose original abundances cannot be recovered from scale metadata alone. Ordinary processing converts to the algorithm's working domain and restores the input scale. Filters return subsets of the original assay without a numeric round trip. These conventions apply to legacy experiments, glyco subclasses, and plain SummarizedExperiment objects wherever the operation supports them.

Working domains

  • Raw abundance: total-area, median, absolute-median, median-quotient and quantile normalization; MissForest and half-sample-minimum imputation; aggregation (including custom f); low-expression, variance and CV filters; total-intensity and CV plots. Custom aggregation callbacks receive raw values after missing values are removed. A sum over an all-missing group is zero, represented as -Inf on ordinary log scales.

  • Log2 abundance: loess and robust-regression normalization; KNN, BPCA, PPCA, SVD and MinProb imputation; rank abundance, intensity boxplots, RLE, PCA and replicate scatter plots. RLE subtracts the row median in this working domain.

Batch detection and correction both use log2(raw + 1e-6). Correction reverses this offset and truncates negative corrected abundances to zero (-Inf on ordinary log scales). Skipped or failed corrections keep the original assay exactly.

Missingness and constancy are evaluated in the current representation. Sample-minimum imputation also uses the current representation; wholly missing samples remain missing. Half-minimum imputation likewise leaves wholly missing samples missing.

Log-like coordinates

"logx" denotes log-like coordinates whose original abundance cannot be recovered from the scale alone. Supported algorithms use these coordinates directly, including legitimate negative values and zeros. No logarithm, exponentiation, pseudocount, or automatic CLR recentering is applied.

logx supports quantile, loess and robust-regression normalization; KNN, BPCA, PPCA, SVD, MissForest and sample-minimum imputation; missingness and constant-variable filters; batch detection/correction; missingness, intensity, RLE, PCA and replicate plots; and annotation. Suitability of each model for particular CoDA or VSN coordinates still depends on the data.

Operations requiring recoverable abundances reject logx: total-area, median, absolute-median and median-quotient normalization; half-minimum and MinProb imputation; low-CV, variance and expression filters; aggregation; TIC, CV and rank-abundance plots; and repeated CoDA or VSN transformations. impute_zero() accepts only raw. zero_to_na() replaces zero on raw and -Inf on ordinary log scales, preserving finite coordinate zero and other non-finite values; it rejects logx.

Transformations and automatic processing

transform_clr(), transform_alr(), auto_coda() and normalize_vsn() accept ordinary scales and deliberately produce scale = "logx". CoDA returns log2-ratio coordinates and VSN returns its log-like coordinates. CoDA requires finite, positive abundances (finite ordinary log input), with no missing values. Other log-domain algorithms require finite observed coordinates; use zero_to_na() and suitable imputation or filtering first.

Automatic functions keep their existing algorithm selection and inherit that algorithm's scale policy. auto_clean() and auto_normalize() reject logx; auto_impute() rejects it when its selected algorithm is MinProb. Pipelines store the actual processing function and parameters and perform no hidden scale conversion. ALR fallback records CLR, restarting from the supplied seed so its history faithfully replays the fallback transformation.

Protein adjustment has a separate abundance contract; see adjust_protein(). Its scale API is unchanged by this adaptation.
